activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-6t-6)\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-6t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =(1)^{3}-3(1)^{2}-6(1)+C \\ 0 & =1-3-6+C \\ C & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the skateboarder at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-6t+8.$

To find the time interval in which the skateboarder is moving to the *left*, we must solve the inequality $v<0.$ This gives

$$
{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-6t+8=(t-1)({t}^{2}-2t-8)<0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t)$, we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094076/assets/c86cdd70316b0bdb620a9a3224823be70069328e0aac83d2c0add2b925323423.png)

From the graph, we see that $v<0$ whenever $1\,<\,t\,<\,4.$
